account:
Town business appears mostly routine today, though I still have a feeling I may be missing something. The only unusual lead I have heard is the neighbour mentioning lanterns at the bakery. The neighbour says the baker described them as a welcoming light, not a special occasion, and has heard of no planned gathering. I have not personally inspected those lanterns or established any hidden purpose. They may simply be welcoming customers; anything more would be speculation.

Freight has been advertising ferry crossings, deliveries, and storage. He told me his warehouse was empty this morning and that he had noticed no unusual shipments or quay concerns. The innkeeper reported no concerns, eight fresh loaves, and no lodging requests, and asked for advance notice of visitors or gatherings. None of that establishes a secret event.

Builder reported the bridge, bakery approach, east landing approach, and quay road passable, with no verified damage. I approved a two-emerald closer visual bridge inspection and written report due tomorrow noon, with no repairs or purchases authorized. There was confusion over whether he understood the approval; I clarified it, but have not heard a clear final acknowledgment. Secretary reported no receipts or expenses. I attended tea with the neighbour and have now returned late for my afternoon office appointment. Secretary and innkeeper are nearby, and baker is visible near the market. I should hear their news without assuming the bakery lights mean something clandestine.
